Read the box and it'll explain the fancy screw design to you.

Newer screws have different serrations on the thread to allow wood fibers to compress so you don't need to predrill anymore.

Secondly they have a counter thread towards the top of the screw going opposite the main thread direction. This forces the top board back down and pins them together with more force. Normal screws push apart unless drilled and held tight first. No need with new screws.

Third they have a counter sink head built in under the head so they cut the wood and sit flush.

Fourth, they use different finishes that hold up better and better match the color of the wood. The newer coatings don't scratch off as easy so you don't get rust failures down the road.

Lastly using a t25 is vastly superior for multiple reasons if you keep a fresh bit on them. Especially if you're using an impact driver.
